original_test_intent: Inject the approved uncorrectable completion-timeout condition on a mapped PCH PCIe switch port and verify the exact CTE status, bounded non-fatal/recoverable behavior, applicable management/indicator response and complete endpoint recovery.
original_method: The FAE maps the physical PCH endpoint to port and X/Y registers, identifies the authoritative CTE status register and severity/mask, confirms the package's `uce` selection, performs one injection, correlates raw register and Windows AER evidence with endpoint/link recovery, then restores settings under OOB supervision.
manual_activity: The FAE must resolve the CTE register conflict, approve the PCH port/X/Y and severity, execute one UCE and own endpoint recovery. The agent can collect raw registers and correlate Windows/link evidence only.
required_inputs: PCH endpoint/BDF to Cscript port and pcieX/portY map
Authoritative CTE register/bit (ERRUNCSTS versus source ERRCORSTS), severity and mask policy
ITP/CScripts build/hash and proof `uce` injects the intended CTE
Windows AER, link/device recovery and applicable BMC/UEFI/front-panel oracle
Endpoint quiesce, OOB console, abort, recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated/quiesced PCH endpoint with independent console
Stop before injection until the CTE register and severity are authoritative
One mapped injection with raw before/after register/link captures
Abort on wrong bit, fatal escalation, host reset, link/device loss or failed recovery
No automatic retry; preserve evidence and restore settings
agent_execution_scope: Validate supplied map and collect read-only raw register, Cscript, Windows, link/device and management evidence
Do not choose register/port/severity, change BIOS, inject, reset/retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Resolve ERRCORSTS versus ERRUNCSTS and CTE semantics
Define recovery and conditional log/indicator expectations

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic PCH logs cannot establish CTE or resolve the register contradiction; Windows conflicts with dmesg.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not use the source oracle until the owner identifies the correct CTE status register. Then run `injectPcieError_pch(...,'uce')` only on the mapped port with proven CTE semantics and severity.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: PCH UCE/CTE intent, normal recovery, conditional indicators and 15/10-minute estimates are preserved; register and port are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture authoritative uncorrectable-status/severity/mask and link state, inject one mapped CTE, correlate the exact raw bit with Windows AER, measure endpoint/link recovery, preserve optional management/indicator evidence and restore/diff state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects the acceptance path only after engineering decides which register is authoritative; it does not rewrite Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic UCE or an ERRCORSTS read cannot prove the intended completion-timeout status if CTE is in ERRUNCSTS.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong port, register interpretation or severity can hide failed injection, reset an essential PCH device or crash the host.

review_improvement: Surfaces a direct corrected-versus-uncorrectable register contradiction that would otherwise let the wrong register or a missing injection appear successful.
independent_technical_reasoning: The expected CTE bit is the core oracle, yet the source directs an uncorrectable event to a corrected-status register while the detailed eDPC row names ERRUNCSTS. That is not a harmless placeholder: reading the wrong register could falsely report failure or conceal another bit. The exact register, severity and PCH target must be owner-approved before one destructive injection. Since these are resolvable platform inputs, RPUC remains correct instead of BLOCKED.
